annotation.title_clean: Toward a Fourth Law of Robotics: Preserving Attribution, Responsibility, and Explainability in an Algorithmic Society
annotation.title_en: Toward a Fourth Law of Robotics: Preserving Attribution, Responsibility, and Explainability in an Algorithmic Society
annotation.summary_en: Response essay to Jack Balkin's three laws of robotics for an Algorithmic Society. Pasquale frames them as regulation of regulation, broadens methods for identifying algorithmic nuisance beyond cost-benefit analysis, and proposes a fourth law requiring attribution of robotic and algorithmic actions to responsible humans or organizations, preserving accountability and explainability.
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes a fourth law of robotics: robots and AI systems must indicate the identity of their creator, controller, or owner (attribution).
Supports Balkin's information fiduciary and public duty laws for algorithm users.
Software and devices replacing professionals should face equivalent fiduciary standards.
Cost-benefit analysis is manipulable; other methods are needed to identify algorithmic nuisance.
Warns exculpatory clauses in legal software terms extinguish accountability litigation.
